thread:
maya: heads up — canary on gpu-pool-7 is showing a p95 regression for the /chat/produce route after yesterday's kernel upgrade. +120ms vs baseline.
raj: saw alerts. can you paste the quick profile snapshot? which kernel version?
maya: kernel v2.15.0 (was v2.14.3). profile snippet below — numbers are canary vs baseline:
```
route: /chat/produce
kernel: v2.15.0
baseline p50/p95/p99: 30ms / 120ms / 300ms
canary  p50/p95/p99: 34ms / 240ms / 410ms
kv_cache_hit_rate: 86% -> 62%
avg_batch_tokens: 48 -> 92
microbatch_count_avg: 3.0 -> 1.8
queue_dequeue_latency_ms: 8 -> 22
```
sasha: that avg_batch_tokens jump is wild. did the rollout flip batching policy?
maya: yes — we enabled batch_on_full_token_budget and bumped default token_budget for "prod" tier as part of the rollout. suspect interaction: larger batches + kernel prefetch changes -> more KV cache churn -> misses -> kernel prefetch stall -> higher p95.
lucas: two hypothesis: 1) kernel v2.15 changed prefetch heuristics that amortize cost only at larger batches; 2) token_budget increase causes fewer but larger microbatches which spikes live KV misses. both amplify latency.
raj: can we try keeping kernel v2.15 but constrain token_budget targets per route/tier? also consider switching queue policy to EDF to prioritize short-deadline requests.
maya: agreed. planning a canary with these changes: rollback batch_on_full_token_budget, and apply dynamic token targets per route/tier. config sketch: 
```
dynamic_token_budget:
  routes:
    /chat/produce:
      prod:
        target_tokens: 64
        max_tokens: 96
        algorithm: slo_p95
      canary:
        target_tokens: 48
        max_tokens: 80
  defaults:
    target_tokens: 40
    max_tokens: 96
queue_policy:
  algorithm: EDF
  soft_cutoff_ms: 18
  stall_threshold_ms: 100
kernel_selection:
  prefetch_threshold_tokens: 70   # prefer prefetching kernels if batch_tokens > 70
  metric: prefetch_cost_per_token
```
raj: add metric hooks: prefetch_cost_per_token, kv_miss_penalty_ms, and batch_token_distribution. run 1-hour canary and capture p50/p95/p99 + kv hit curve vs sequence length.
sasha: also enable short-term kv-cache pinning for tokens in prefix windows to reduce churn for long sequences. we can try a 30s pin TTL for canary routes.
perf-bot: auto-rollback: p95 breach threshold triggered at 1767894389 — canary rolled back by deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: rollback executed (auto) — reason: p95 > target by 2x.
maya: OK thanks. i'll prepare the constrained token-target canary and EDF queueing test. goal: p95 < 160ms and kv_hit > 75% for /chat/produce.
lucas: if that works, we should bake dynamic defaults into the rollout process: any kernel change that also alters prefetch heuristics must run with conservative token budgets for 24h.
raj: sounds good. maya, ping when the canary is up and include perf-bot traces. :eyes:
maya: will do — starting run now, posting logs in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
